question: Public authorities often procure comparable goods, services and works, but the data needed to compare prices, contract values, variations and final expenditure is not consistently available or interoperable. This limits the ability of Member States to identify abnormal costs, weak scoping, inefficient purchasing or recurring overruns. 1.
Does the Commission consider that better procurement data could support cost benchmarking across comparable public contracts in Member States?
Will the Commission assess whether current procurement data standards are sufficient to allow comparison of planned contract values, modified contract values and final expenditure?
Will the Commission consider supporting EU-level guidance or tools to help public authorities benchmark procurement costs and identify areas where public spending efficiency could be improved?
